01 / The problem

The dogs who don't make it aren't failing.
The systems around them are.

4 of 5
dogs in rural county shelters will not find veterinary care or adoption.
“Gigi’s serves the rural shelters everyone else drives past.”

02 / Our thesis

Access saves more dogs.

It isn't just about building more shelters, or rescuing one dog at a time. It's connecting everything it takes into a single system — getting dogs out of rural areas, vet care, behavior help, adoption, and the research behind it. When care reaches the places everyone drives past, we save more dogs.

03 / How the system works

A hub in the middle.
A network around it.

Dogs come in from rural county shelters in Appalachian Ohio into one central care hub in Columbus. From there we place them through trusted adoption partners across the region — Columbus, Dayton, Cleveland, and Detroit — so no single shelter gets overwhelmed. One system, built to grow across the Appalachian region.

Intake — rescue from five rural Appalachian counties into Gigi's.
Placement — out to partners across Ohio and into Michigan.

04 / The founding principle

Our system is already built — so every gift saves more dogs.

Gigi's was founded by George and Tina Skestos in honor of their dog, Gigi — an Akita. The mark at the top of this page is her.

The founders funded the buildings, the equipment, and the team up front — so when you give, 100% goes to the dogs.

Funders call this catalytic giving1: building the systems an organization stands on, so it can create lasting change instead of just meeting this month's crisis.

Your gift doesn’t build the system — it runs it. Every dollar saves more dogs.

1. The concept of catalytic philanthropy was introduced by Mark R. Kramer, “Catalytic Philanthropy,” Stanford Social Innovation Review (Fall 2009).

06 / How we deliver

One mission.
Four service pillars.

The model becomes real in four working service lines — who we serve, and what we deliver.

01 · SHELTER SERVICES

A full-scale rescue model — and a learning lab.

Who we serve

Municipal shelters in rural Appalachian Ohio, and the rescues that support them.

What we deliver

We rescue by transport, carry the whole care journey, and place dogs through metro adoption partners. What we learn becomes the playbook — and our Van Grant program funds partner shelters’ own transport, every van running our GET Protocol.

1,400+ dogs rescued a year
50,000+ animals reached through 24 partner vans

02 · RESCUE VET SERVICESGigi’s Rescue Veterinarians

Low- and no-cost vet care for the groups doing the work.

Who we serve

Nonprofit rescues, shelters, and government partners.

What we deliver

Surgery, preventive care, diagnostics, and infectious-disease treatment — including our parvo ICU — priced so the organizations saving dogs can afford to save more of them.

2,800+ dogs given low-cost care & surgery a year
9,800+ free vaccines · 90% parvo survival

03 · BEHAVIOR SERVICESGigi’s Behavior

High-quality behavior support, at every stage.

Who we serve

Families, adopters, rescues, and veterinary referrals.

What we deliver

Veterinary behavioral medicine, one-on-one behavior consultation, and classes — judgement-free, from first puppy class to the hardest cases.

2,000+ families supported a year

04 · RESEARCH & EDUCATION

Evidence the whole field can use.

Who we serve

The sheltering field — shelters, rescues, and the vets who serve them.

What we deliver

We study what actually saves dogs — parvo treatment, transport stress, behavior, access — then publish it and teach it, so every shelter can save more dogs.

Peer-reviewed research, published
GET Protocol adopted across the partner network

Four pillars, one system — and every stage stays connected.

07 / Research & education

Research is part of the model —
not a side project.

It runs across all four pillars, and the goal isn't only better outcomes inside Gigi's — it's a stronger sheltering system everywhere. Led by Dr. Herron, with Drs. Hadden, Sheaffer, and Gilbert-Gregory contributing and publishing alongside Gigi's veterinary team — two of them veterinary behaviorists. The Ohio State University College of Veterinary Medicine supports select studies.

Shelter dogs are treated in a field with far less research funding, fewer clinical trials, and less shared data than human medicine. That gap costs time, money, and lives. Gigi's exists to figure out what actually works — and prove it.

Human medicine has a research engine.
Shelter dogs need one too.

Research studies submitted to each field’s leading journals every year — a rough measure of how much research each one gets.

Gigi’s built this comparison by selecting the leading journals in each field — human medicine (NEJM, JAMA, The Lancet, BMJ) and veterinary medicine (JAVMA, AJVR, JVIM). It’s an illustration of the scale of the research gap, not a complete count of every study in either field — and shelter-dog research is a small slice of veterinary medicine’s.

Peer-reviewed · 2024

Gabapentin for canine behavioral disorders

Peer-reviewed · 2026

L.I.F.E.™ — Gigi's own behavior evaluation

Original Gigi's research: a validated tool that reads how a dog actually lives in the shelter — not how it reacts to artificial tests — to find the dogs who need help coping.

09 / Where we're going

Our vision.

A stronger, more effective sheltering system where every dog has access to the care and support they need to thrive.

The home campus hub in Columbus is a template, not a destination. Once it's financially self-sustaining, Gigi's is built to inspire, build, and lead additional new hubs like this one — each one funded to sustain itself, so one region's success pays for the next.

01
Establish the home campus hub.
02
Build and optimize transport, care, and outcome systems.
03
Achieve home campus hub financial independence.
04
Engage community and political leaders in state and national conversations on shelter reform.
05
Support scalable, sustainable rural shelter models.

National leaders like the ASPCA and Best Friends Animal Society have shown the country what large-scale animal welfare can achieve. Gigi's is pursuing that same mission from a different foundation — a self-sustaining, systemic model that builds local capacity and empowers the communities it serves to lead.

Appalachia runs thirteen states deep — from New York to Mississippi, through Kentucky and Tennessee.
The model is built to follow the need — and stay focused on Appalachia.
